_comment: SHARED FIXTURE - one answer key for the DocStore subsystem, all four frameworks.
DocStore is the PUREST test of ADR-0024 in the whole framework, because
substitutability IS its feature: 'develop against a zero-dependency local
SQLite store and switch to MongoDB in production by setting one env var'.
Every other subsystem merely aspires to the swap - this one advertises it.
It is also the subsystem with the least evidence. The last measured finding
below is the one that explains all the others: NO DocStore test in ANY of the
four frameworks has ever touched a real Mongo collection. The substitutability
promise has zero coverage, so nine defects accumulated behind a green suite.
These are INVARIANTS, not a bug list. Nine defects were measured 2026-08-01.
HOW THIS IS CHECKED: see scripts/audit-contract-fixtures.py. An empty 'cases'
list means OWED. Note that for THIS fixture, 'owed' is the entire point - the

invariants.rule: When a Mongo URI is configured and the driver is present, get_collection() returns a REAL Mongo collection. It never silently returns the local SQLite fallback.
invariants.why: MEASURED: on a default PHP production install TINA4_MONGO_URI is honoured by isServerless() - which reports 'not serverless' - while getCollection() still hands back local SQLite. The two disagree, so the app reports it is on Mongo while writing to a container-local file that vanishes on the next deploy. Production writes are lost with no error at any point.

invariants.rule: URI configured + driver absent produces the SAME outcome in all four frameworks, and that outcome is loud. It must not silently degrade to the local file.
invariants.why: MEASURED: one env produces THREE different outcomes - Python, PHP and Ruby silently degrade to the local SQLite file, Node crashes. Silent degradation here means production traffic writing to a local file nobody is reading. ADR-0024 rule 3: a provider that cannot honour an operation must RAISE, naming the provider and what is missing.
cases: a missing driver raises instead of using the local file
the same uri with the driver present still selects mongo
the message does not leak the uri credentials
invariants.status: PROVEN in all four 2026-08-04 (ADR-0033), re-measured first at v3 HEAD (python 75cb10b, php 867838a5, ruby b15749c, nodejs b23bf29) and unchanged since 2026-08-01: python, php and ruby silently returned the local SQLite collection; node threw a bare ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND naming an npm package rather than the framework decision. PHP had a SECOND door nobody had opened - ext-mongodb PRESENT with the mongodb/mongodb library absent (its real `composer install --no-dev` shape) made isServerless() report FALSE while getCollection() still returned SqliteCollection, the two disagreeing exactly as a-configured-uri-selects-the-real-provider forbids. All four now raise DocStoreDriverMissing at provider RESOLUTION, before any socket, with one message shape naming the env var that supplied the URI and never its VALUE (a Mongo URI carries user:password@; each suite asserts the leak negatively). is_serverless() became CONFIGURATION-ONLY in python, php and ruby - node already had those semantics and was right, so for once the master moved to match it. TESTED WITHOUT MOCKS in genuinely driverless environments: python a bare `python -m venv` with no pymongo; php `php -n` for the extension and a DocStore-only bootstrap for the library; ruby GEM_HOME/GEM_PATH at an empty dir with bundler's env scrubbed; node the module built into a directory outside the repo where `mongodb` is unresolvable, which is what `npm install --omit=optional` gives. Each probe reports whether it really was driverless, so a leaky environment FAILS rather than proving nothing. Mutation-proved in all four: removing the named raise, and reverting is_serverless() to driver-presence, each turn the suite red. NOT DECIDED HERE, and recorded as owed: DocStore has NO zero-dependency wire-protocol fallback in ANY framework - the hand-rolled OP_MSG transport exists only in the session handlers (python, php, nodejs) and PHP's cache backend - so the three-state model collapses to two, symmetrically, and no framework was made to degrade to match another.

invariants.rule: Every method and cursor operation available on the fallback exists with the same name and meaning on WHAT get_collection RETURNS for the real provider, and vice versa. Code written against one runs unchanged against the other. Where the driver lacks a method, Tina4 MAY supply it on BOTH sides via a delegator - never on the fallback alone.
invariants.why: MEASURED: PHP's every result accessor and the whole cursor chain is call-site incompatible with the real driver, and THREE of them fail SILENTLY as null. Ruby's find_one() does not exist on Mongo::Collection, and the cursor's two-argument sort(key, direction) is rejected by the driver. The swap is advertised at the call site and broken at the call site.
cases: the driver spelling works on both providers
the uniform spelling works on both providers
the fallback surface resolves on the wrapped driver
invariants.status: PROVEN in php + ruby 2026-08-03 (ADR-0025), RE-PROVEN against the WRAPPED surface 2026-08-04 (ADR-0035). Python already satisfied it - its fallback is a perfect subset of pymongo. Node is OWED: its divergence is the sync/async one below, and ADR-0035 deliberately does NOT restore Node's cursor [Symbol.iterator]/toList() because a real FindCursor is async-only. The comparison target CHANGED: ADR-0025 compared the fallback against the RAW driver, so a method the driver lacked could only be deleted; ADR-0035 compares against what get_collection RETURNS, which lets a delegator supply the method on both sides instead. Ruby wraps Mongo::Collection in MongoCollection and its View in MongoView; PHP wraps MongoDB\Collection in DocStoreDelegator. Measured 2026-08-04 against a real MongoDB: 0 fallback-only COLLECTION methods in both, with aggregate/bulk_write/indexes/watch/withOptions all still reachable through the delegator - the objection ADR-0025 raised against a hand-written FACADE, which does not apply to a delegator. Two divergences were recorded here as OPEN when ADR-0035 landed and are now CLOSED by ADR-0036, which is a separate invariant below (the-cursor-chain-is-deferred-and-works-on-both-providers): the PHP fallback Cursor carried sort/limit/skip that MongoDB\Driver\Cursor does not have, and the Ruby fallback Cursor's two-argument sort(key, direction) was rejected by Mongo::Collection::View#sort. PHP's find() is now DEFERRED and Ruby's MongoView#sort normalises all three spellings, so the PHP canary in this invariant that pinned ['sort','limit','skip'] as fallback-only now asserts [].

invariants.rule: find() returns a chainable query that ACCUMULATES sort/limit/skip and executes only when iterated or materialised - never inside find() itself. sort() accepts a field plus a direction, a list of [field, direction] pairs, OR a field => direction map, and all three mean the same thing on both providers.
invariants.why: MEASURED 2026-08-04 against a real MongoDB 7.0.39: the framework's own DOCUMENTED example, find([...])->sort('total', -1)->limit(10), worked on the SQLite fallback and FATALLED on the real provider with 'Call to undefined method MongoDB\Driver\Cursor::sort()'. PHP's driver takes sort/limit/skip as find() OPTIONS and hands back an already-executed cursor, so by the time find() returned there was nothing left to chain. A published example that does not run is an ADR-0025 defect and a First Principle violation at once. Checking the whole grid rather than the reported symptom found a second defect underneath: the MAP sort spelling worked on every driver and RAISED on the fallback in THREE frameworks (php TypeError, node 'keyOrList is not iterable', python 'too many values to unpack'), while Ruby's fallback accepted all three and its DRIVER rejected two of them. 10 of 32 provider/spelling combinations failed.
cases: the cursor chain works on both providers
invariants.status: PROVEN in all four 2026-08-04 (ADR-0036). 32/32 identical on both providers after the fix. php's find() on the Mongo path returns a DEFERRED DocStoreQuery that accumulates the chain and calls find($filter, $options) ONCE at materialisation; ruby's MongoView#sort normalises all three spellings to the driver's single spec document; node and python needed only the map/dict spelling on their fallbacks, because a real FindCursor and a pymongo Cursor are both already lazy and chainable - those two are the shape the other two were brought to. PYTHON IS THE MASTER AND PYTHON WAS BROKEN on the mapping spelling; it was FIXED here rather than mirrored into the other three. The case asserts more than the happy path: skip composes with sort and limit, an ASCENDING sort actually ascends (a direction that was ignored outright would pass a descending-only test), and the chain is LAZY - a document inserted after the chain is built but before it is iterated must appear, which a query executed inside find() would fail. Mutation-proved: removing the deferred options turns the MONGO path red while the fallback stays green, which is the asymmetry that made this invisible for the whole of v3. The PHP harness canary that pinned ['sort','limit','skip'] as fallback-only under ADR-0035 now asserts [].

invariants.rule: A call returns the same KIND of thing on both providers. If one returns a value and the other a promise, un-awaited code silently changes meaning when the env var changes.
invariants.why: MEASURED: in Node the fallback collection is fully SYNCHRONOUS while the driver is fully ASYNCHRONOUS. Un-awaited code returns a real value locally and a Promise in production - so `if (doc)` is true for every query, and a missing document reads as found. The type changed underneath identical source.
cases: for-await over a cursor yields the documents
invariants.status: PROVEN in nodejs 2026-08-03 (ADR-0025 clause 3). Node-only by construction: python, php and ruby have a SYNCHRONOUS driver, so there is no sync/async axis for the fallback to diverge on. Each case asserts on BOTH providers.

invariants.rule: A filter that matches on one provider matches on the other. Array-containment semantics in particular behave the same on the SQLite fallback as on Mongo.
invariants.why: MEASURED: array fields do not match on the SQLite fallback - Mongo's array-containment semantics are absent in ALL FOUR frameworks. A query that returns documents in production returns nothing in development, or the reverse, with no error. Unanimous across the family, which marks it as a contract never written down.
cases: array queries match identically on both providers
invariants.status: PROVEN in all four 2026-08-03 (ADR-0025 clause 4). EIGHT array-query behaviours diverged IDENTICALLY in all four - three of them FALSE POSITIVES where the fallback matched a document Mongo excludes. Fixed by implementing Mongo's rule over json_each: a condition on an array-valued field matches when ANY ELEMENT matches, a negation when NO element does. The test asserts the two providers return the SAME counts rather than a hard-coded number, so it cannot drift.

invariants.rule: Repeated get_collection() calls do not create unbounded client connections. Clients are reused or closed.
invariants.why: MEASURED: a new Mongo client is constructed on EVERY get_collection() call and never closed, so connections grow without bound - on the real provider ONLY. The fallback has no connections, so this is invisible in development and exhausts the server in production. A resource leak that only exists after the swap.
cases: repeated get collection does not grow connections
invariants.status: PROVEN in all four 2026-08-03 (ADR-0025). Fixed in node, python and ruby by caching one client per (uri, database); php was ALREADY bounded because ext-mongodb pools at the libmongoc level, and is asserted anyway so that correctness-by-accident cannot regress silently. Each suite drives 3 rounds + 100 further calls and asserts the growth PLATEAUS - a pool flattens, a leak keeps climbing.

invariants.rule: A type the DocStore module exports for use in documents can be encoded by the real driver.
invariants.why: MEASURED: the ObjectId class the DocStore module exports cannot be encoded by the real driver. The framework hands the developer a type and the production provider rejects it - so the documented way to construct an id works locally and fails after the swap.
cases: the exported object id is usable as a document id
an object id round trips through its string form
invariants.status: proven in python; owed in php, ruby, nodejs

invariants.rule: Every framework has at least one DocStore test that runs against a REAL Mongo collection, not only the SQLite fallback.
invariants.why: MEASURED, and this is the root cause of the eight rules above: NO DocStore test in ANY of the four frameworks has ever touched a real Mongo collection. The entire substitutability promise has zero coverage, which is exactly how nine defects accumulated behind four green suites. The no-mock rule already forbids substituting a double for a real dependency; this states the positive obligation.
